News.title: Reeves paves way for new drilling in North Sea as Iran war energy shock sees fuel prices skyrocket
News.content:
RACHEL Reeves has ramped up plans for new drilling in the North Sea to boost oil and gas supplies amid the fallout from the Iran war.

The Chancellor wants to press ahead with unlocking billions of extra oil barrels to save relying on costly overseas supplies.



She said it was the “quickest way” to bring on stream more supplies as households and families are hit by the energy price shock.



The move allows for “tie backs” which would see more fossil fuel extraction adjacent to existing fields.

Reeves, speaking from Washington DC, said: “We’re now working through pretty intensely the technical details with the energy companies.

She added: “What tie backs are is where you use existing infrastructure to exploit sort of larger geography of oil and gas is the quickest way to bring on stream more oil and gas.

“It’s important we get the detail right so that companies have the confidence to exploit those resources.”

Motorists have been hit hard by the rising costs of petrol and diesel since the US went to war with Iran.

The knock-on effects have also been

It comes as Energy Secretary Ed Miliband is also under pressure to give the go-ahead to the Jackdaw and Rosebank, which would be the first major projects to be approved in ten years.

Reeves has previously said she would be “very happy” to support extraction at the two sites to boost “jobs and tax revenue”.



Miliband is expected to make a decision on the Rosebank oil field and the Jackdaw gas field.

The Cabinet Minister has previously said that the only way to “get off the rollercoaster” is to abandon oil and gas altogether.

Labour’s manifesto before the last election said they would not issue new licences to explore new fields in the North Sea.

But the government are under intense pressure to boost energy security after oil and gas prices surged after US-led attacks in Iran.

Any such move would boost tax revenues to the Treasury and be backed by unions in a bid to save thousands of jobs.

News.title: Teacher, 31, faces life in jail over string of 25 rape & sex abuse charges involving two student victims as young as 10
News.content:
PROLIFIC ATTACKER Teacher, 31, faces life in jail over string of 25 rape & sex abuse charges involving two student victims as young as 10

AN elementary school teacher is facing life behind bars after being hit with rape and sexual abuse charges involving students.

Marisa Noel was clapped in handcuffs and charged on Monday following a two-month investigation into her behaviour with a fifth grader at Teche Elementary School.





The 31-year-old was then accused of further, more serious charges after another victim was identified.

The former Louisiana teacher will now stand trial for a total of 25 charges, including first-degree rape.

If convicted, Noel could receive a life sentence in accordance with state law.

Authorities have not revealed the exact ages of the victims but at least one was in the fifth grade.



This would likely mean they are either ten or eleven years old.

The second set of charges included ten counts of indecent behaviour with juveniles and two counts of having child sexual abuse material.

She has also been accused of unlawful communications and harassment, as well as using a computer to solicit a minor.

Noel is now being held at St. Martin Parish Correctional Center, records show.



This is not the first time a teacher has been accused of wildly inappropriate behaviour with pupils.

Earlier this week, a married school social worker narrowly avoided jail time after pleading guilty to sexually assaulting an underage student.

Chloe Rose Castro was sentenced to 20 years to life of Sex Offender Intensive Supervision Probation (ISP) after having a sexual relationship with a sixth-grade boy.

The 29-year-old will also serve three years in community corrections before probation.

Appearing in mugshots wearing pigtails, she must also register as a sex offender for life.



The victim will also receive $14,000 in restitution.

Castro was taken into custody after the victim’s parents notified the Arvada Police Department back in October 2024.

They handed over evidence that showed the former social worker engaging in an inappropriate relationship with their child.

An affidavit revealed the child’s parents discovered inappropriate Instagram messages between their son and Castro.

When the boy’s parents tried to take his phone from him, the child quickly logged out of all his accounts and changed his passwords.

“There is no sentence that I could ask for which will give the community their trust back in Jefferson County Public Schools,” the prosecutor said in court.

“There is not a sentence that will take away the trauma this child suffered.

News.title: You could be fined £2,500 for flying the England flag at your house on St George’s Day – know the rules in full
News.content:
ST GEORGE’S Day is just a week away but patriotic Brits could face fines if found to be breaking certain flag laws.

Households may be hit with a hefty penalty of up to £2,500 for incorrectly displaying the England flag.



According to local council planning laws, only one flag on a vertical flagpole attached to the roof of a building is allowed.



If the flagpole is attached to the side of the building, the flag must not be larger than 2 square meters in size.

Refusing to obey council requests to remove an oversized flag could lead to households being reported and fined.

This means for those wanting to display a larger banner, they will need to fly it directly from their roof.

These rules apply to any country’s national flag, including both flags of St George and St Andrew.

Consent may also be needed for those living in a controlled area, such as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Fines can start as low as £100 to £250, with a maximum penalty of £2,500 for repeated offences.

It is also against the law to “display any  or subject matter additional to the design of the flag,” according to government guidance.

It adds: “Two flags on the same flagpole projecting from any part of a building are permitted provided one of the flags is from category (a) (flags which do not need consent) such as a national flag and that flag is flown in the superior position.



“Otherwise, only one flag on a projecting flagpole on a building is permitted. The flag may not exceed 2 square metres in size.”

St George’s Day will fall on April 23 this year, as an annual celebration marking the death of the patron saint in 303 AD.

News.title: Trump’s war secretary Pete Hegseth leads prayer by ‘quoting the Bible’ – but it’s really from iconic Pulp Fiction scene
News.content:
PETE Hegseth mistakenly quoted an iconic scene from Pulp Fiction instead of the bible while leading a prayer at the Pentagon yesterday.

The US Defence Secretary urged Christians to pray with him while discussing the rescue mission of a US fighter pilot stranded in Iran.





But his appeal backfired after he misquoted a biblical verse using lines from the iconic Quentin Tarantino movie instead.

Hegseth said: “You will know my call sign is Sandy 1 when I lay my vengeance upon thee.”

The actual bible verse from Ezekiel 25:17 pledges “great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes”, which was changed by director Tarantino.

The altered version is righteously delivered by Samuel L. Jackson’s character in the movie just before he shoots a man to death.

Hegseth told listeners that the prayer was recited by the recent “Sandy One” Combat Search and Rescue (CSAR) mission to rescue a downed airman Iran.

“They call it CSAR 25:17, which I think is meant to reflect Ezekiel 25:17,” he said.

Hegseth earlier vowed that the US was “locked and loaded” to resume combat as the clock ticked down to the end of the shaky Iran war ceasefire.



Military chief General Dan Caine added that forces, including thousands of newly-arrived troops, were “ready to resume major combat operations at literally a moment’s notice”.

US military Centcom chiefs said an Iranian cargo ship was among at least 13 vessels forced to turn back by US battleships blockading the paralysed Strait of Hormuz.

A spokesman said the “Iranian-flagged cargo vessel” attempted to evade patrolling warships by skirting the Iranian coast as it navigated the strait.

It performed a swift U-turn when confronted by the USS Spruance guided-missile battleship and headed back towards the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas.

Centcom stressed no vessels entering or leaving Iranian ports have made it past US forces since the start of the blockade on Monday.



But the 24-mile oil artery – carrying a fifth of the world’s crude supplies – also remained shut down to other vessels threatened by the rogue state yesterday.

Peace talks aimed at ending the economically crippling 49-day war will resume in Pakistan next week.

Talks are also planned between Israel and Lebanon – which harbours Iran-backed Hezbollah – for the first time since 1993.

But the spectre of bloody escalation remains – along with World War Three fears – as Iran continues to defy Trump demands to scrap its nuclear aims and stop funding terror.

Around 6,000 more US ground troops were heading to the war zone yesterday aboard the USS George H W Bush aircraft carrier and its escort ships.



They will join 4,200 amphibious troops aboard the USS Boxer from the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit expected before the end of the month.

Around 3,500 troops on the USS Tripoli recently entered the war zone supported by 3,000 crack airborne troops already flown to within striking distance of the front line.

It comes after Pope Leo launched an extraordinary attack on “tyrants” who spend billions on war in a thinly-veiled blast at Donald Trump.

The pope hit back after days of abuse from the US president who has branded him “very weak” and accused him of thinking “it’s OK for Iran to have a Nuclear Weapon”.



Leo said on a visit to strife-torn Cameroon: “The world is being ravaged by a handful of tyrants.The masters of war pretend not to know that it takes only a moment to destroy, yet often a lifetime is not enough to rebuild.”

Trump turned on the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics – including 70 million in the US – after Leo declared the Iran War “truly unacceptable” last week.

He also described Trump’s recent threat to destroy “an entire civilisation” in Iran as morally indefensible.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump posted a messiah-like AI image of himself healing a man on his sickbed after the row broke on Monday but took it down following a backlash from outraged Christians.

America’s Bible belt voters make up a crucial tranche of his support and he later attempted to assure them the image showed him posing as a doctor.

News.title: Moment grinning, wide-eyed woman clings to bonnet of moving car & says ‘go on you stupid dog’ in bizarre road rage clash
News.content:
THIS is the moment a crazed woman clings to the bonnet of a moving car in a bizarre road rage clash.

The shocking dashcam video shows the deranged woman shouting horrid abuse at the young driver who then speeds along a motorway with the woman still attached to her car.





Aspiring Australian para-Olympian Natalie Alice Shaw, 22, says she was turning into a car park in July last year when another vehicle driving the wrong way blocked her.

The driver of the other car pulled over and got out to confront Shaw.

In a selfie video, Shaw explains: “She comes and she’s in front of my car and she goes, ‘What are you going to do? Hit me?'”

“And I was like, ‘Well, yeah if you’re in my way, I’m gonna get you to move out of my way’.”

The woman then jumps onto Shaw’s bonnet and starts swearing at her.

“Are you going to hit me? Go on,” the unknown woman can be heard saying in the footage.

“Go on c***, go on you stupid dog.”



In 9News’ footage, Shaw recalls swerving in an attempt to get the woman off the front of her car.

Shaw starts picking up speed and eventually reaches about 37mph.

The woman tries to stay on the bonnet by holding onto the window wipers.

She is heard screaming: “Slow the f*** down c***.”

The woman then loses her grips and falls from the moving car.



“She went flying off the side of the road. Oh my god,” Shaw said.

Shaw has been charged with dangerous operation of a motor vehicle and she lost her lost her licence for six months.

During sentencing the magistrate said it was the most bizarre behaviour she had seen in 25 years of practice.

“The behaviour of the complainant was erratic, it was dangerous, it placed you in danger, you also placed her in danger,” Thompson said.

“It was a poor decision that you made in the circumstances, being confronted with what anyone objectively would see as a terrifying situation.”



Shaw’s dreams of competing at the LA Paralympics in 2028 could now be in jeopardy.

News.title: Lidl air fryers are rejected at UK border as they could EXPLODE – with shoppers warned over ‘serious risk of fire’
News.content:
AN AIR fryer sold by Lidl has been rejected at the UK border over concerns that it could explode.

Shoppers have been warned of its “serious risk of fire” due to its electrical components.



The Silver Crest Air Fryer has been rejected from being imported into the UK as it did not meet the necessary electrical requirements.



The electrical appliance has been sold through Lidl to customers.

The product is made in China and is described as a black electric air fryer with attached wall plug.

But the common home appliance, model JD989A, has been stopped at the border over fire concerns.

In a government-issued notice, the Office for Product Safety and Standards rejected the product from entering because its fuse link had no granular filler.

As well, the plug face of the appliance did not meet the dimensional requirements.

It said that the product presents a “serious risk of fire” with the plug possibly overheating and exploding.

Air fryer are a compact countertop kitchen appliance designed to simulate deep-frying without submerging food in oil.

It works as a powerful convection oven, using a heating element and fan to circulate hot air rapidly around food, producing a crispy exterior with minimal or no oil.



But they are known to catch on fire from overheating and cause the plastic components to burn.

The Sun has approached Lidl for comment.

News.title: Vile elderly couple who hurled racist abuse at nurse and yanked her hair in shocking attack in park are jailed
News.content:
A VILE couple who hurled racist abuse at a nurse in a shocking attack caught on camera have been jailed.

Fyona Bairstow, 72, and Michael Bairstow, 77, abused Apple Moorhouse in a park in Halifax after she told them their dog should be on a lead.





Michael Bairstow told the Filipino NHS worker to “go back to your dinghy”, while his wife pulled her ponytail when she tried to walk away.

Shocking footage, which later went viral, also showed the couple throwing water over Apple while yelling “ban immigrants”.

The couple have now been jailed for eight weeks each after they pleaded guilty to racially aggravated assault.

Michael Bairstow also admitted assaulting another woman who tried to intervene.

Sentencing, chairwoman of the bench Gill Arnold asked the couple to stand, saying: “I just want to have a look at you… That kind of attitude and those words and the things you said to Ms Moorhouse, is not something that comes out of the blue in a second, it’s something deeply rooted.

“That somebody can be so vile and aggressive to somebody such as this young woman here – I can only think you must be extremely ashamed.”

Bradford Magistrates’ Court heard the row erupted at Manor Heath Park in Halifax last August when nurse Apple confronted the pair after their dog spooked her six-year-old daughter.



Sneering Michael Bairstow ordered his dog to “get her, kill” and threw a bottle of water over her.

He then mocked small boat migrants by making rowing gestures and asking: “Have you got a rubber boat? Did you come across the Channel?”

Disturbing footage also showed Fyona Bairstow confronting the nurse as she filmed the abuse.

The thug was captured grabbing Apple’s arm and trying to snatch her phone.

She then threatened: “I’ll make you so bloody sick you’ll wonder what the hell is going on.”



The violence escalated further when a female passer-by stepped in to try to stop the row.

Michael Bairstow punched her in the face and snarled: “Sticking up for immigrants, who do you think you are?”

In a victim impact statement, Apple said the couple immediately became “very hostile” after she asked them to control their dog.

She added: “When I tried to walk away the female pulled me back by my ponytail causing my head to go backwards.”

“They were very racist towards me – they seemed to want to make everything a conversation about immigrants – and calling me a slave.”



Speaking outside court, Apple, who is a British citizen, said she had felt less safe after the incident and “keeps looking over my shoulder”.

She continued: “I feel anxious obviously, every time that I think back, I feel upset,” she said. “It’s a big thing, racism, and it needs to be dealt with.

“I’ve been here since 2009 and never had anything like this before. For 10 years, it was fine but now it’s got worse.

“I used to work in healthcare and I wanted to go back but I felt scared… this happened and I just didn’t go back.

“Caring was my passion but then this happened and it was hard to go back.”

News.title: Can I appeal a primary school place? Your legal rights if your child does not get their top choice TODAY
News.content:
PRIMARY school offer day is here, and while many will be ecstatic about getting their preferred school, many will be less than pleased and want to appeal.

National Offer Day is today, and this will mean that across England, parents will be finding out whether their children will be attending the primary school of their choice.



How will I find out about my offer?

Local authorities will send offers by email for parents who applied online, while those who applied by paper may receive a letter in the post in the coming days.



Parents can also log in to their local authority’s online admissions portal to check their offer directly.

Unfortunately, some families will be disappointed to learn they were not offered the primary school that they wanted.

Thankfully, there is an appeal process that allows them to provide evidence that could see their child enrolled in time for September.

How are primary school places decided?

Competition for the best schools is high each year, and places are given by local authorities using each school’s published admissions criteria.

When a school is oversubscribed, it must rank children in order of priority using specific criteria.

Children who are or have been in care are the highest priority, followed by those who already have siblings at the school.

The next criterion is children living within the school’s catchment area, and if there are still too many applicants, distance from school is often used as a tiebreaker, with those living closest given priority.

There can also be faith-based requirements for some religious schools.



How to appeal primary school place

The letter or email you receive about your offer will give exact details on how to appeal. If you have multiple applications turned down you will have to appeal against each rejection separately.

You can only appeal once against each rejection and you will have at least 20 school days to appeal from when the decision letter is sent.

Each local authority will set a deadline for submitting information and evidence to support your appeal for the school you were rejected from.

Don’t leave appealing too late, however, as anything submitted after the deadline may not necessarily be considered and could result in delaying your hearing.

Some charities will be able to give you legal advice about the appeals process and your rights during your appeal.



When you will get a hearing

If a formal appeal for a primary school place is submitted, you will be entitled to a hearing before an independent panel.

You will be given at least 10 school days’ notice of a hearing and they will take place within 40 school days of the deadline for making an appeal.

This panel will be made up of three or more individuals with an educational background, who will decide if the school’s admission criteria were followed correctly when your child was rejected.

During the hearing, you will have an opportunity to give your reasoning as to why your child should be admitted to the school.

If your reasons for admission outweigh the school’s reasons for not admitting any more children, or your child, your appeal will be upheld.



If the criteria were not properly followed or do not comply with the school’s admissions code, your appeal also must be upheld.

The hearing could take place in person, via a video call, telephone call or, in some cases, based on written submissions.

Despite your child being measured against multiple criteria, it is worth noting that 92.6 per cent of families in England were offered their first choice of primary school in 2025, according to the Department for Education.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And while it can be concerning that your desired school has initially rejected you, 98.3 per cent of families in England received an offer for one of their preferred schools during the same year.

Not all appeals are successful, however, and appeals may be denied in reception, year 1 and year 2, if all the classes already have 30 children.

News.title: Teen planned massacre at Wales school as police uncover chilling manifesto
News.content:
Teen planned massacre at Wales school as police uncover chilling manifesto

Theodore Hopes, 18, spoke about 'planning a school shooting' before police found a host of disturbing material on his phone, including videos of himself making a Nazi salute

View 2 Images The Newtown College campus in Newtown, Wales (Image: Google Maps)

A teenage Hitler fanatic who threatened to kill people at his college was caught with a chilling 'Mass Murderer' manifesto and videos of himself performing Nazi salutes.

‌



Theodore Hopes, 18, made a comment about "planning a school shooting" when armed police visited his father's house in Llandrindod Wells, Wales, on December 8 last year, where they seized an air rifle which turned out to be a legally-owned. The teenager was taken to the local Brecon police station, where a healthcare practitioner treated a small cut to his hands after he punched an oven.

‌



A sentencing hearing at Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court today heard a number of items belonging to Hopes were seized, including a phone filled with images of Samurai swords, a video of the defendant watching videos of Adolf Hitler and making a Nazi salute, an English translation of Mein Kampf, visits to gun and air rifle website.

‌



View 2 Images The case was heard at Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court (Image: South Wales Echo)

Other disturbing material included websites selling human skulls and bones, research on pipe bombs, mass suicides, secondary school attacks, terrorist attacks, and press reports about school knife attacks. Hopes, of Broadway House, Llandrindod Wells, pleaded guilty to making threats to kill, reports Wales Online.

The defendant was asked by the healthcare practitioner who treated his cut if he self-harmed and if he had made previous attempts on his own life. Asked if he wanted to kill people, Hopes replied: "I can't. They have taken my gun away from me but I can still go in and stab people."

‌



Prosecutor Jason Howells said the 18-year-old claimed he "dreamed about killing people" and wanted to go into Newtown College, which he attended, and "shoot people". When asked who he wanted to shoot he gave a name but did not elaborate further. When asked if he wanted to kill himself he said: "Suicide by police".

The practitioner said the defendant spoke in a "calm, cold, and matter of fact way" and seemed "dead behind the eyes". When interviewed, Hopes said he had no recollection of the conversation and had no plans to carry out a "school shooting".

A search of Hopes' mobile phone uncovered a nine-page document called 'Theo Hopes Mass Murderer,' which was addressed to political parties, media organisations, and the Dyfed-Powys Police and Crime Commissioner. The subheading read: "Manifesto, the end of Theo Hopes."

‌



In his sentencing remarks, Recorder Paul Lewis KC said it was the defendant's intention the document would be sent to the recipients following the "commission of a serious crime and [Hope's'] ultimate death".

The court heard Hopes was of previous good character. In mitigation Martha Smith-Higgins said her client was a young man who was "remorseful".

She said the defendant accessed the material due to him being "isolated" as a result of his mental health issues and use of alcohol and drugs. Two referrals had been made to Prevent in an attempt to stop him from looking at such material, and the teeanager has been prescribed medication.

Article continues below

Sentencing Recorder Lewis said the defendant's attitudes had been described as "misogynistic and far right". The judge added: "You have developed troubling and potentially dangerous thoughts and ideas. You are a young man with troubled attitudes and beliefs. You have a fascination with weapons, bombs, school attacks, and Nazi materials."

Recorder Lewis said the defendant had already served three and a half months in custody and the best way to deal with him was through probation.

Hopes was sentenced to a two-year community order with a 30-day rehabilitation activity requirement. He was also made subject to a prohibited activity requirement for 12 months, which would require his phone and sim card to be monitored by probation.

News.title: KLM cancels flights to and from UK as major airlines face fuel crisis
News.content:
KLM cancels flights to and from UK as major airlines face fuel crisis

KLM is set to cancel more than 100 flights due to the fuel crisis sparked by the war in Iran

View 2 Images KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is the flag carrier of the Netherlands (file) (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

A major European airline is set to cancel more than 100 flights - including services to and from London - due to rising fuel costs linked to the war in Iran.

‌



KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, the flag carrier of the Netherlands, will cancel 160 flights over the coming month, split evenly between departures and arrivals at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol. The airline said it is not facing jet fuel shortages, but has taken the decision as a cost-containment measure due to rising fuel prices.

‌



“Passengers affected by these changes will be rebooked onto the next available flight. As these are destinations KLM serves multiple times a day, such as London and Düsseldorf, travellers can usually be accommodated quickly," the airline said.

‌



"KLM expects a busy May holiday period and is making sure passengers can travel to their holiday destinations as planned." The cancellations account for about one per cent of KLM’s European schedule.

View 2 Images The US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has raised concerns about the price and availability of jet fuel (Image: Getty Images)

‌



It comes as airlines across Europe cancel routes to manage higher operating costs.

Earlier this month, UK airline Skybus, which operated daily flights between London Gatwick and Newquay, cancelled all future flights due to the rising price of fuel and a drop in passenger numbers.

Skybus had operated the flights since November 2025 under a Public Service Obligation funded by Cornwall Council and the Department for Transport, which had been scheduled to run until May 31. The airline's last services took place on April 2.

Article continues below

Skybus managing director Jonathan Hinkles said at the time: "The huge rise in the global cost of fuel following the conflict in the Gulf, coupled with a significant drop in new passenger bookings since mid-February’s announcement of the planned closure of the PSO air route, forms an insurmountable barrier to the service continuing through April and May.

"At a time of great economic uncertainty and steps being taken to conserve energy worldwide, it is neither environmentally nor economically sound for us to continue flying with vastly reduced passenger numbers."

News.title: Snooker legends turn out to mourn John Virgo at emotional cathedral service
News.content:
Snooker legends turn out to mourn John Virgo at emotional cathedral service

The service was held two days before the start of this year's snooker World Championship. Virgo died at his home in Mijas Costa, Spain, aged 79, in February

View 6 Images Jimmy White gave fans a thumbs-up on arrival at the service (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Snooker's biggest stars came together to pay tribute to John Virgo at a moving church service.

‌



Virgo, widely known as JV, was remembered fondly during an hour-long memorial at Sheffield Cathedral almost two months after he died aged 79 at his home in Mijas Costa, Spain.

‌



Legendary players Stephen Hendry, Steve Davis, Jimmy White, Dennis Taylor, John Parrott and Ken Doherty were among a plethora of famous pals who attended the event alongside Virgo's family, including his widow Rosie Ries and his grown-up children Gary and Brook-Leah.

‌



Six-time world champion Davis said: "We're going to miss him dearly. A great commentator but a good friend to us all, he made you feel very special.

"We all thought we were friends with John because he had a great heart and he was funny, sometimes cantankerous but we loved him for that.

"All in all, he was part of snooker's furniture, he was part of snooker's history and a wonderful commentator. He got the best out of every match."

‌



John Virgo was looking forward to huge milestone before sudden death says pal Dennis Taylor READ MORE :

View 6 Images John Parrott arriving at the memorial (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Bishop of Sheffield Pete Wilcox officiated the service, which included a choir singing hymns and other songs, including their own version of the Beatles' hit Here Comes the Sun. Other songs included There Is a Higher Throne by Keith Getty, Remember Me by Bob Chilcott and Morning Has Broken.

Taylor, Hendry, Parrott and Doherty spoke about Virgo from the altar, with Parrott telling the congregation his old pal is now “in the great commentary box in the sky with his good friend Willie Thorne, who we lost a few years ago.” He described Virgo as "irreplaceable" and "always the ultimate pro" and admitted: “I’m gonna miss him like mad.”

‌



View 6 Images Stephen Hendry pictured outside the cathedral after the service (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Referencing one of Virgo's most famous commentary phrases "is there a gap?", Parrott said: “Is there a gap… there is now my friend.” He added: “Thanks for 40 years of friendship, camaraderie and for making our wonderful sport just that bit better. Goodnight JV."

Doherty, who won the 1997 World Championship, said Virgo "left an indelible mark on the sport of snooker” and "was the life and soul of our group". He added: "I loved him dearly. He was like a big brother, almost like a father to me."

‌



Hendry told how he first began listening to Virgo's commentary when he was aged just 13 before later enjoying the privilege of working with him as a co-commentator. He added he will miss him, as will the sport, but they will "soldier on". Taylor told the congregation: “It’s not going to be the same.”

View 6 Images Cliff Thornburn and Dennis Taylor arrived together (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Standing in front of a huge black and white photo of his father at the front of the altar, Virgo's son Gary gave an emotional, and amusing, eulogy to his father. In it, he charted how his dad, who he said was a life-long Man Utd supporter and keen horse-racing fan, rose from "simple beginnings" in Salford as the son of a crane driver dad and stay-at-home mum before becoming one one of snooker's biggest stars.

‌



He also described how his dad transcended the sport by becoming a household TV name alongside comedian Jim Davidson on hit BBC TV show Big Break and his commentary catchphrases, including 'where's the cue ball going' “became part of the fabric of the sport”. But he added: “At his core he only remained what he’d been from the very beginning - just a lad from Salford who loved snooker.”

Virgo's daughter Brook-Leah read a touching poem, which included the lines: "The baize are quiet, the lights are low, a legend has left us, it was such a sudden blow”. It also included the words: “Where’s the cue ball going we heard him call, with a twinkle in his eye as he loved it all.”

And it added: “The waistcoat is hung up. The cue is hung up, he gave snooker his very best. His spirit will live on in every single play. The entertainer supreme. Rest in peace JV, our incredible dad and their incredible grandad.”

‌



View 6 Images John Virgo's widow Rosie Ries and his daughter Brook-Leah were seen supporting each other (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Ken Doherty also read the Henry Scott Holland poem Death is Nothing At All, while six-time world champ Steve Davis read a Bible reading from the Book of Revelation.

Other well-known faces in the packed congregation included former stars Cliff Thorburn, Tony Knowles and Peter Ebdon, as well as current players John Higgins, Mark Williams, Shaun Murphy, Neil Robertson, Mark Allen and Stuart Bingham.

‌



Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan was unable to attend, but World Seniors Snooker chairman Jason Francis told the congregation Ronnie had told him “John was like a second father to him.” He added: “I witnessed in Spain his grief at losing JV.”

The service was organised by snooker MC Rob Walker, who also spoke during it paying tribute to Virgo, telling how he "opened up the sport to a whole new appreciative audience".

The service was followed by a reception at Sheffield Town Hall and came two days before the start of this year's snooker world championship. Speaking afterwards, Jimmy White, who spoke at a previous funeral service for Virgo held in Spain, told the Mirror: "The service was absolutely fabulous. They did a fantastic job. It was an honour to be here."

‌



View 6 Images The order of service for the event at Sheffield Cathedral (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Jimmy added: "I'd known him for 50 years and 47 of those years we were very close friends and I loved him with all my heart and I know he loved me. I'll miss him every day."

Snooker fans had been allowed to join the church congregation on a first-come, first-served basis. They included Phil Hudson, who travelled from Telford.

Article continues below

Phil, who was wearing a t-shirt paying tribute to Virgo, said: “I just wanted to pay my respects to him really. He was a great man, he’ll be truly missed."

Snooker fan Jim Fitzpatrick, 65, from Doncaster, who was wearing a top decorated with a snooker table and Virgo’s name, said: “I wanted to pay my respects to John. As far as I was concerned he was Mr Snooker. A legend. He was so funny and witty and made snooker so interesting.”

News.title: Government ADMITS Mandelson failed security vetting  - but says Starmer not aware
News.content:
Government ADMITS Mandelson failed security vetting - but says Starmer not aware

No10 was rocked by the revelation that the disgraced peer had been rejected by security officials before his appointment as the UK's representative in Washington

View 2 Images Peter Mandelson failed security vetting before becoming the UK's ambassador in Washington (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Peter Mandelson was appointed as the UK's 'Trump whisperer' despite failing his security vetting, the Government has admitted in a hammer blow to Keir Starmer.

‌



No10 insisted that the PM was not informed that security officials had rejected Mandelson's clearance before he was dispatched to Washington last year. It emerged on Thursday that officials in the Foreign Office took the extraordinary step of overruling the UK Security Vetting (UKSV) decision so the appointment could go ahead.

‌



UKSV oversees high-profile and sensitive appointments and identifies potential security risks. Downing Street said in a statement that the PM was unaware Mandelson was rejected until this week, and had planned to update the Commons.

‌



The extraordinary chain of events, first reported by The Guardian, has been met with anger by MPs, with the Foreign Office now facing calls to explain itself.

Speaking to reporters in Washington DC, Chancellor Rachel Reeves appeared to suggest Mr Starmer and former Foreign Secretary David Lammy should have known. She said: “I didn’t know anything about the vetting process. I’m the Chancellor, I’m not the Foreign Secretary, and I’m not 10 Downing Street, so I can’t give you any more information on that.”

A government spokesman said no ministers were aware, pointing the finger at mandarins in the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). In a statement No10 said: “The security vetting process for Peter Mandelson was sponsored by the FCDO. The decision to grant Developed Vetting to Peter Mandelson against the recommendation of UK Security Vetting was taken by officials in the FCDO.

‌



Ex-cop MP shares harrowing frontline experiences as he makes emotional plea READ MORE :

View 2 Images Keir Starmer has faced a huge backlash over Mandelson's appointment (Image: PA Wire)

“Neither the Prime Minister, nor any Government Minister, was aware that Peter Mandelson was granted Developed Vetting against the advice of UK Security Vetting until earlier this week.

“Once the Prime Minister was informed he immediately instructed officials to establish the facts about why the Developed Vetting was granted, in order to enact plans to update the House of Commons."

‌



The rejection came after the PM had already announced Lord Mandelson was to be the UK's man in Washington to help handle unpredictable US President Donald Trump. Mandelson was sacked in September last year after emails were published throwing new light on his relationship with convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

The day before Mandelson's sacking, on September 11, the PM told the Commons at PMQs, in response to a question by Kemi Badenoch: "As the right honourable Lady and the House would expect, full due process was followed during this appointment, as it is with all ambassadors."

And at a press conference in February, Mr Starmer told reporters that Mandelson had been cleared by the security services. He said: "There was a due diligence exercise that culminated in questions being asked... the answers to those questions were not truthful."There was then security vetting carried out independently by the security services... which gave him clearance for the role. Clearly, both the due diligence and the security vetting need to be looked at again."

‌



Mr Starmer has vowed to be transparent, and the Government is committed to releasing all documents relating to Mandelson's appointment. In a landmark vote forced by the Tories, MPs backed a humble address demanding the files are released.

But The Guardian reported that senior officials within the Government have been weighing up withholding documents which reveal Mandelson was not given vetting approval.

The statement continued: “The Government is committed to complying with the Humble Address in full as soon as possible. Any documentation within the scope of the Humble Address that requires redaction on the basis of national security or international relations will be provided to the ISC. This will include documents provided to the FCDO by UK Security Vetting.”

‌



Dame Emily Thornberry called for MPs to be told the truth after it was reported that Lord Peter Mandelson failed his security vetting but was still appointed ambassador to the US. The senior Labour MP and chairwoman of the Foreign Affairs select committee posted on X: "My committee asked several times whether red flags had been raised by Peter Mandelson's vetting process.

"It seems there were. Who overrode these concerns? Why were we kept in the dark? People need to stop messing us about and tell us the truth."

The peer - who resigned from the House of Lords earlier this year - took up the role in February 2025, but lasted just seven months after emails showed he had coached Epstein following his conviction for a child sex offence.

‌



In January this year, more documents were released from the US Department of Justice's Epstein files, including emails suggesting he leaked sensitive information to the billionaire financier. Mandelson was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, and remains on bail.

At the time of his appointment David Lammy was Foreign Secretary and Sir Olly Robbins was the top civil service in the Foreign Office. Mr Starmer's former chief of staff, Morgan McSweeney, quit in February over his role in the process.

In a letter to the foreign affairs committee in September, current Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper and Sir Olly wrote: "The vetting process was undertaken by UK Security Vetting on behalf of the FCDO and concluded with DV clearance being granted by the FCDO in advance of Lord Mandelson taking up post in February."

‌



The letter made no mention of Mandelson failing UKSV's vetting process. A source close to Mandelson claimed the axed ambassador had no knowledge of this matter.

During the vetting process, individuals are quizzed on relationships which could be used maliciously against them, as well as associations that could have an inappropriate influence.

They are also asked about their financial arrangements, social media profiles and time spent overseas.

‌



Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said: “Keir Starmer had already made a catastrophic error of judgement. Now it looks as though he has also misled Parliament and lied to the British public. If that is the case, he must go.

“Labour came into Government on a promise to clean up politics. Instead we’re seeing the same old sleaze, scandal and cover-ups as we did under the Conservatives.”

And Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch posted on X: "Last September, Keir Starmer told Parliament three times that `full due process' was followed over the appointment of Lord Mandelson.

‌



"We now know the Prime Minister misled the House. The Prime Minister must take responsibility."

In February Mr Starmer told the Commons that Mandelson had lied throughout the appointment process. He said: "Mr Speaker, he [Mandelson] lied repeatedly to my team when asked about his relationship with Epstein before and during his tenure as ambassador.

"I regret appointing him. If I knew then what I know now, he would never have been anywhere near government."

Article continues below

The Mirror has contacted the Foreign Office, the Cabinet Office and Lord Mandelson's representatives for comment.

News.title: Moment killer dad whines about handcuffs after murdering premature baby daughter
News.content:
Moment killer dad whines about handcuffs after murdering premature baby daughter

Evil Sean Jefferson, 35, moaned about his handcuffs being 'too tight' as police arrested him for subjecting his five-week-old daughter to extreme and repeated violence - which ultimately killed her

Bodycam shows killer father Sean Jefferson threaten to report officers

A dad who killed his five‑week‑old daughter by subjecting her to extreme and repeated violence complained about his handcuffs being "too tight" when police tried to arrest him.

‌



Evil Sean Jefferson was today jailed for a minimum of 22 years after he murdered little Darcy-Leigh Jefferson, who suffered dozens of injuries to her head, ribs and legs before dying from a catastrophic brain injury on March 29, 2022.

‌



Jefferson, 35, was told to "calm down" as he began lashing out at two arresting officers, threatening to report them after his "hand was hurt" while they detained him. The killer had called 999 two days earlier on March 27, 2022, telling the operator his baby had "stopped breathing".

‌



View 5 Images Baby killer Sean Jefferson moaned about his handcuffs being too tight (Image: Staffordshire Police / SWNS)

Darcy, who was born five weeks premature, tragically died in hospital on March 29. Throughout her short life, she was repeatedly assaulted and sustained 47 rib fractures, as well as fractures to her legs.

Police bodycam footage captured the moment Jefferson became increasingly agitated as he was handcuffed for his crimes. "That's a bit tight, that is mate. Look at that, see that?," he told officers. "That's very tight. Can you please loosen it?"

‌



View 5 Images Jefferson was told to 'calm down' as he began lashing out at officers (Image: Staffordshire Police / SWNS)

The officer told Jefferson to "stay still then", only for him to demand his badge number and say: "I'm putting in a complaint about you. Simple, done. You're hurting my hand, mate."

He was then told to "calm down", but demanded police "take it off then, hurry up." He added: "I want your name and badge number, you're abusing your rights now, mate. Simple."

‌



View 5 Images Jefferson was today jailed for a minimum of 22 years (Image: PA)

Darcy-Leigh's mother, Amy Clark, 34, was jailed for seven years after being found guilty of causing or allowing the infant's death - conduct the sentencing judge attributed to substance abuse.

The court heard that Clark had been struggling in the lead-up to Darcy-Leigh's death and had sent Jefferson text messages expressing her exhaustion and his failure to provide support. He fired back with a message threatening to "put you 6ft underground" if she killed her baby through excessive drinking.

‌



The trial also revealed that both parents were using drugs throughout their daughter's brief life. Neither chose to give evidence in their own defence.

View 5 Images Darcy-Leigh Jefferson died after being repeatedly assaulted (Image: PA)

Both Clark and Jefferson had denied multiple charges throughout the nearly two-month trial, which concluded last month.

‌



Jefferson, of Birch Court, Walsall, was also convicted of two counts of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, in addition to murder.

Clark, from Lichfield, Staffordshire, had charges of murder or manslaughter dropped by prosecutors towards the end of the trial. Alongside her conviction linked to the baby's death, she was further found guilty of two counts of causing or allowing serious harm to a child.

View 5 Images Amy Clark was sentenced to seven years (Image: Staffordshire Police / SWNS)

Article continues below

A "complex and challenging" investigation by Staffordshire Police's Major Investigations Department, supported by the Crown Prosecution Service, found that Darcy died as a result of a catastrophic head injury - but that this was not an isolated act of violence.

Senior Investigating Officer, Detective Chief Inspector Ian Fitzgerald, of our Major Investigations Department, said the behaviour of Darcy-Leigh's parents represented an "appalling betrayal of parental responsibility".

He further stated: "Jefferson will now spend a significant part of his life in prison but no sentence can ever reflect the cruelty inflicted on Darcy or repair the devastation left behind."

News.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire deal struck and Donald Trump claims it will begin tonight
News.content:
Israel-Lebanon ceasefire deal struck and Donald Trump claims it will begin tonight

US President Donald Trump claims ten day stop in missile exchanges agreed between Israel and Lebanon - even though it was without mention of Hezbollah, which was actually fighting Israel

View 6 Images US President Donald Trump claims ceasefire (Image: Salwan Georges - Pool via CNP/Shutterstock)

US President Donald Trump has claimed a ten day ceasefire has been struck between Israel and Lebanon. Trump wrote on social media: “I just had excellent conversations with the Highly Respected President Joseph Aoun, of Lebanon, and Prime Minister Bibi Netanyahu, of Israel.

‌



'These two Leaders have agreed that in order to achieve peace between their countries, they will formally begin a 10 Day ceasefire at 5 P.M ET .” The two countries had their first meeting in 34 years in Washington DC, along with US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio.' It means the ceasefire starts at 10pm London time.

‌



View 6 Images Israel's Netanyahu, America's Trump and Lebanon's Aoun (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It is not believed there has been confirmation of a ceasefire from Israel, Lebanon or Hezbollah, the latter being the party that is at war with Israel. Trump’s claims come as the US is working on setting up a second round of talks with Iran to end the war in the Middle East.

Pakistan's army chief met with Iranian officials in Tehran on Thursday in a bid to ease tensions in the Middle East and arrange a second round of negotiations between the US and Iran. It follows almost seven weeks of war in Iran which has hit much of the region and a deepening crisis in the Strait of Hormuz as the US tightened its naval blockade.

View 6 Images Israeli troops in Upper Galilee, near Lebanon border (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Britain 'likely' to face Russian attack following Kremlin warning READ MORE :

As many as 20 ships have now been turned back to Iranian ports by the fleet and it is believed only Chinese vessels have slipped through the Iranian blockage of the waterway. The White House said any further talks with Iran would likely take place in the Pakistani capital of Islamabad.

More than 10,000 American troops are helping enforce the blockade on Iranian ports although no ships have yet needed to be boarded. Abdul Malik al-Houthi, leader of the Iran-backed Yemeni Houthis rebel group, said that in negotiations with Iran, the U.S. is making "impossible demands for any independent country to accept."

View 6 Images Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon (Image: ATEF SAFADI/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



He said the ongoing two-week ceasefire was a result of "failures" by the U.S. and Israel to achieve their goals in the Iran war. The current cessation of hostilities between the US and Iran started on April 8 and ends on April 22.

Al-Houthi said: "If negotiations succeed, it will either result in a longer period of stability or an end to the aggression.” More than 2,000 people have been killed in Lebanon and over one million displaced by the fighting.

View 6 Images Israeli helicopter fires machine gun at southern Lebanon (Image: ATEF SAFADI/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



Lebanon's Health Ministry says that among the killed are 260 women and 172 children since the latest war between Israel and Hezbollah began March 2. Another 7,185 have been wounded.

Israel's latest military escalation started after Hezbollah fired rockets towards northern Israel in solidarity with its key ally and patron Iran. U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters at the Pentagon that Iran "ultimately needs to come to the table and make a deal."

View 6 Images Israeli troops on Lebanon border (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

"We'd prefer to do it the nice way through a deal led by our great vice president and negotiating team. Or we can do it the hard way.” Iran has repeatedly insisted that it doesn't seek a nuclear weapon and that its program is for peaceful purposes. And a deal that is being discussed is for a ten to 15 year delay to Iran having nuclear capability - very similar to the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action struck by President Obama - the JCPOA - which Trump tore up.

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor could lose further honour amid Epstein fallout
News.content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor could lose further honour amid Epstein fallout

A major corporation said it has written to the disgraced ex-prince and asked him to give up an honour he inherited through his father Prince Phillip, which would see Mr Mountbatten-Windsor lose one of his few remaining titles

View 3 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been asked to give up a major honour (Image: AP)

Disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been urged to relinquish one of his few remaining titles amid the fallout around the ex-prince's relationship with paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

‌



Elected members of the City of London Corporation have written to the ex-Duke and asked him to give up the freedom of the city honour, which he received in 2012. The group added that Andrew inherited the honour "by virtue of patrimony" because his dad, the late-Prince Phillip, was formerly a freeman.

‌



The corporation added that inheriting the honour was a "legal right", adding that there was no legal route for it to be stripped from him.

‌



View 3 Images The ex-prince has had most of his titles and honours stripped from him in recent months (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

This honour is a ceremonial title which has historically allowed recipients to walk sheep over London Bridge.

In a statement released on Thursday, a spokesperson said: "Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor received the freedom of the City of London in 2012 by virtue of patrimony, which is inherited as the child of a freeman and constitutes a legal right.

‌



"Applications via patrimony are not considered or endorsed by our elected members, and there is no effective legal mechanism to remove this type of freedom.

"Elected members have today agreed to write to Mr Mountbatten-Windsor, inviting him to formally relinquish the freedom. They will consider the response received, if any, at a future meeting and determine what action may be taken."

View 3 Images Prince Philip, with Queen Elizabeth, on his way to receive the Freedom of the City of London in 1948 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Other famous people to have received the award include comedian Sir Lenny Henry, Hollywood star Cate Blanchett, Footballer Harry Kane and boxer Frank Bruno. All of Andrew’s siblings – including the King – also have freedom of the city of London.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor has always vigorously denied any wrongdoing in his connection with Jeffrey Epstein.

The former prince was stripped of all of his royal titles, styles and honours by King Charles last year as more details about his relationship with the convicted paedophile came to light.

‌



One of the City of London’s ancient traditions, the freedom is believed to have begun in 1237 and enabled recipients to carry out their trade. Typically, the honour is awarded to people nominated by corporation councillors.

This comes weeks after Andrew's ex-wife Sarah Ferguson was stripped of her "Freedom of the City of York" honour after a unanimous vote, in March. She and Andrew were given the honour as a wedding present from York in 1987 during a visit to the city.

It was another humiliation following the mounting pressure on the ex-royal for her ties to Epstein, who she once described as the "brother I always wishes for". She has denied all allegations. Andrew was also stripped of the "Freedom of the City of York" honour in 2022.

Article continues below

If the former duke agrees to relinquish the London honour, it will be another in a string of titles he has lost over his association with Epstein.

Andrew was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office. He spent 11 hours in custody, on his 66th birthday, before he was released under investigation.

News.title: British burger giant falls into administration as five London restaurants close
News.content:
British burger giant falls into administration as five London restaurants close

London-based burger chain MEATliquor has entered administration after 17 years in business as the restaurant industry faces rising energy prices and operational costs

View 3 Images MEATliquor has officially appointed administrators (stock) (Image: d3sign via Getty Images)

A much-loved British burger chain MEATliquor has now entered administration after closing a number of restaurants.

‌



London-based chain has officially appointed administrators, according to The Gazette, delivering a devastating blow to devotees of its renowned burgers and beers.

‌



The chain, operated by Meatalier, had cultivated a dedicated following amongst Londoners. Last month MEATliquor closed five of its eight London locations - including outlets in Islington, Clapham Junction and Queensway. Just three premises remain open - two in Oxford Circus and East Dulwich, plus its sister sports bar BLOODsports in Covent Garden.

‌



The move follows rising energy prices and soaring operational costs. Founder Scott Collins previously cautioned the sector was facing immense pressure.

View 3 Images MEATliquor is facing rising energy costs (Image: Google Maps)

Airline files for bankruptcy as flights cancelled – but vital firm may be saved READ MORE :

He told Restaurant Online: "On top of VAT, rates, beef and energy costs, we've now got a new war creating uncertainty and more Tube strikes to deal with. We're in the same position as a lot of others in the industry and I'm just getting ahead of things before we're forced to."

‌



The burger brand was first launched in 2009 by Yianni Papoutsis and business partner Collins. What began as a modest mobile van, the MEATwagon, rapidly transformed into a thriving restaurant business across London and the South East.

Its first physical store opened close to Oxford Street in 2011, and at its peak the chain had 13 branches - 12 across the UK and one in Singapore.

View 3 Images The burger brand was first launched in 2009 (Image: Google Maps)

Article continues below

This comes as British car dealership is set to close within days. London-based Cargiant will close its site in the capital for good on April 24 after its owners were unable to find a buyer. The company previously had more than 2,000 cars available and was among Britain's busiest used car supermarkets.

The site covers roughly 50 acres and is estimated to be worth around £100m. It sits adjacent to a planned HS2 interchange that will link HS2, the Elizabeth Line, overground and other transport connections.

Cargiant has encountered difficulties in recent years, with directors being compelled to attempt to sell the business and land. The closure follows Cargiant's owners' failure to "secure a viable future for the business".

News.title: Watch: Reporter told to fake domestic abuse claim to remain in the UK
News.content:
Migrants are falsely claiming to be victims of domestic abuse in order to stay in the country, exploiting rules brought in to expedite the process of securing permanent residence for genuine abuse victims

A BBC investigation has found that legal advisers are encouraging some to make up abuse allegations. One of those advisers, Eli Ciswaka, encouraged a BBC reporter to make false allegations of domestic abuse - saying that he would fabricate the claim for £900, creating a story to tell the Home Office in order to secure the client's status in the UK.

Ciswaka did not respond to a written request for comment, but during a phone call to tell him about our investigation he denied being willing to make up a story that the undercover reporter had been a victim of domestic abuse.

Jess Phillips, the minister for safeguarding in the Home Office, said that the abuse of rules around domestic abuse victims was "unacceptable" and that "sham lawyers facilitating this advice abuse will be put behind bars."

Read the story in full here.

News.title: Watch: Reporter told to pose as gay for asylum claim
News.content:
Immigration advisers are encouraging migrants to cheat the asylum system, with some helping migrants to pose as gay to get asylum in the UK, a BBC investigation has found.

A BBC reporter, posing as a former student wanting to remain in the UK, met one of those advisers, Tanisa Khan. For a fee, she offered to provide evidence to support the fake claim that he was gay.

Read more on the first part of a major undercover investigation, in which the BBC reveals how migrants whose visas are due to run out are being given fake cover stories and instructed in how to obtain fabricated evidence including supporting letters, photographs and medical reports.

They then apply for asylum claiming to be gay and in fear for their lives if they return to Pakistan or Bangladesh.

In response to our findings, the Home Office said: "Anyone found trying to exploit the system will face the full force of the law, including removal from the UK."

The new Focker-In-Law trailer has tickled a few eagle-eyed viewers, who have noticed an apparent editing error.

In the movie teaser, dropped Wednesday, Ariana Grande joins the Meet the Parents franchise as Olivia, the soon-to-be fiancée of Henry (Skyler Gisondo), the now-grown son of Greg and Pam Focker, played by returning stars Ben Stiller and Teri Polo.

When Olivia visits Henry’s maternal grandparents — his hard-to-please grandfather Jack (Robert De Niro) and gracious grandmother Dina Byrnes (Blythe Danner) — she quickly wins over Jack, sparking Greg’s jealousy, as it took him years to be accepted into the family.

At one point in the trailer, the family goes for a bike ride. Olivia challenges Greg to a race, and as the two are speeding down the trail, Greg clips Olivia’s back tire, sending her tumbling to the ground.

As she falls on her back, Olivia’s face appears to be that of a stunt double rather than Grande.

open image in gallery Ariana Grande's 'Focker-In-Law' stunt double made an accidental appearance in the trailer ( Universal Pictures )

“The way you can see the stunt double in the [bike] fall scene — I can’t,” one fan commented on YouTube.

“The obvious stunt double is cracking me up lowkey,” a second noted on X.

The Independent has contacted the film’s studio, Universal Pictures, for comment.

Nevertheless, the trailer left many fans impressed and eager for the beloved franchise’s belated return.

“A hilarious comeback for the Focker family, looks like another fun filled comedy just in time for the Thanksgiving holidays,” another said on X, while one admitted: “Looks so much better than I was expecting. They have a great new hook to keep it going and the same energy and chemistry that started it all.”

Focker-In-Law will release in theaters November 25, more than 15 years after the comedy series’s third film, Little Fockers, in 2010. The original film, Meet the Parents, premiered in 2001, followed by the second sequel, Meet the Fockers, in 2004.

The first three films followed the extreme family conflict between the buttoned-up Byrnes and the laid-back Fockers.

open image in gallery Grande stars alongside returning cast members Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro and Teri Polo, in the comedy franchise’s fourth film ( Universal Pictures )

Those three movies were co-written by John Hamburg, who has penned the screenplay for the new film, which he will also direct. Meanwhile, Jay Roach, the director of the initial two titles, Meet the Parents and Meet the Fockers, is attached as a producer. De Niro and Jane Rosenthal will also act as producers through their Tribeca Productions, while Stiller and John Lesher will produce via their Red Hour Films banner.

Grande, 32, was added to the cast last July, hot off the heels of her first Oscar nomination for her supporting role as Glinda in Jon M. Chu’s critically acclaimed Wicked. Gisondo, Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco are also among the new cast.

Following the trailer’s first showing Wednesday at CinemaCon in Las Vegas, De Niro hailed Grande as “probably the single most talented screen partner I’ve been lucky to share the screen with,” to which Stiller replied: “In a way, she’s kind of like the new Ben Stiller.”

De Niro comedically hit back: “She got an Oscar nomination. How many of those do you have?”

Over recent weeks, the England cricket hierarchy has been at pains to show it has learned lessons from a dismal Ashes in Australia. Chief executive Richard Gould, director Rob Key and captain Ben Stokes have led a charm offensive aimed at showing they really do care about county cricket, that they will not be giving failing England players any more leeway, and that preparing for a Test series might actually be a good thing.

Stokes grabbed more attention this week with another interview on the ECB website, in which he insisted his relationship with head coach Brendon McCullum is not strained by a difference of opinion on England’s approach, and that they are “95 per cent aligned”.

All of which has left former England captain Michael Vaughan perplexed. “I have no idea why that interview was released,” Vaughan says. “I don’t think there’d have been one person waking up that morning thinking, ‘Oh, Ben and Baz have got an issue’. Two hours later, that interview gets released, and it’s clear that they’ve had a bit of a problem in the winter.”

Vaughan was not convinced by Key and Gould’s PowerPoint presentation to the media at Lord’s that attempted to lay out England’s next steps and was dismissed as “management speak” in some quarters. “The corporate messaging was just corporate messaging,” says Vaughan. “Slideshows for slideshows’ sake, just to try and prove that they’re becoming more of an attention-to-detail organisation.

“If they really wanted to put on a front, then Ben Stokes, Rob Key and Baz McCullum should have been presenting those slides in front of the media. I have no idea why Richard Gould was talking about cricket. He’s the CEO. He’s what I call the bean counter of the game, and looks after the finances.”

open image in gallery Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum insist they will be keeping a keen eye on the County Championship ( Robbie Stephenson/PA )

The question now is whether England will really change. Can the bridge between the County Championship and the England Test team be rebuilt after it was left to decay for four years?

There are certainly places up for grabs when England take on New Zealand at Lord’s in June, in the first of three Tests. Zak Crawley’s position as an opener is in serious doubt. The bowling unit is not set in stone. Vaughan, who is speaking to promote the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup, a new national hardball competition for state schools, believes there must be changes at both ends of the line-up if England are to start afresh.

“They need tone-setters with bat and ball, so they need someone who opens the batting with Ben Duckett. You can’t expect to be the No 1 team in the world with someone who averages 31 from 64 games [Crawley]. We need to get away from just selecting players because they play in the vibe this era has created. Your opening batters have got to average over 40.

“And then I’d be looking at someone like Ollie Robinson. With the new ball in Australia, they were poor, and they need someone that’s going to set the tone. England needs to sit with Ollie and if it’s a mental thing, if it’s a fitness thing, if it’s an attitude problem that Ollie Robinson has, England have to iron it out. They’re not a good enough team to just put someone like Ollie Robinson on the scrap heap. You look at his numbers in Test match cricket, they’re up there.”

open image in gallery Vaughan at the launch of the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup at Lord’s this week ( Jed Leicester )

There is plenty of time for County Championship players to catch the eye, with four more rounds of games before McCullum and Stokes pick their side. But there is already a familiar name at the top of the run scoring charts: Jamie Smith had an Ashes to forget with the bat and the gloves, but he has made a brilliant start to the season at Surrey, scoring two centuries in two matches batting at three.

The concern with Smith is that his teammate Ben Foakes is Surrey’s preferred wicketkeeper. Smith is likely to retain his place in the England Test team, even after some brainless shots down under, but his glovework needs attention. Vaughan says it is time for him to knuckle down and learn the art of the keeper, even if that means taking matters into his own hands.

“He’s obviously not keeping for Surrey, which is a problem for me. Like Shoaib Bashir, he wasn’t getting in his county team, but he’s [an] England spinner, that can’t be right. But [Smith] should play because he’s too good … His batting’s going to be fine at seven – I’m sure he’ll end up maybe at six in time.

“But I just look at Matthew Prior, when he first started for England as a wicketkeeper-batter, and his keeping was a little bit flawed, and suddenly he went and worked away with [former England wicketkeeper] Bruce French, worked his nuts off every morning and drilled and caught loads of balls and became a brilliant wicketkeeper-batter. I look at Jamie Smith and think, ‘Go on, take a leaf out of Prior’s book’.”

England were criticised for their lack of specialist coaches at the Ashes, with only a temporary bowling coach and no fielding coach on the tour, during which they dropped 18 catches. There was also no keeping coach to work with Smith directly on his struggles behind the stumps.

open image in gallery Jamie Smith has been in sublime form for his county this month ( Getty )

“The coaching has to get better, it’s as simple as that,” adds Vaughan. “Baz McCullum has got to coach the team, and he needs to bring in expertise. And if Jamie Smith is working with Alex Stewart or Bruce French, whoever, Jack Russell, that wicketkeeper coach should be around the England team for the preparation days. And if I was the coach of England, which I’m not, I’d be fine with players bringing in their own coaches to make sure that they’re ready for the Thursday start.

“I’ve never, ever seen a keeper improve by not catching balls. You have to do all the drills. You have to catch loads of balls, and that’s on the Tuesday morning, the Wednesday morning, the Thursday morning, the Friday morning. Every single keeper that I see that gets to the top in their profession are catching balls all the time. I just need to see a bit more of that.”

Over a thousand teams have signed up for the chance to play at Lord’s as stars encourage greater access to cricket in state schools. Find out more here.

Prosecutors in Minnesota have criminally charged a federal immigration officer with assault in what appears to be a first-of-its-kind case following surges of agents into cities under Donald Trump’s administration.

Gregory Donnell Morgan Jr. faces two counts of second-degree assault for allegedly threatening victims with his firearm, according to a criminal complaint announced by Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty on Thursday.

Morgan is accused of speeding up alongside a victim’s car, pulling out a gun and repeatedly pointing it at people inside during a February incident.

Local law enforcement has issued a warrant for Morgan’s arrest.

The charges mark the first against an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer for actions during Operation Metro Surge, which saw hundreds of federal agents deployed to the state for dragnet-like arrests targeting immigrants and protesters.

open image in gallery ( AP )

On February 5, Morgan — behind the wheel of an unmarked rental SUV — was illegally driving on the shoulder of Highway 62 when another car briefly moved into the shoulder to slow him down, according to Moriarty’s office.

When the victim moved back into traffic, Morgan sped up and then matched the pace of the other car, opened his window, and pointed his gun “directly at both victims in the other vehicle while continuing to drive illegally on the shoulder,” her office said.

The charges “reflect an important milestone in our efforts to seek accountability for the harms inflicted on community,” Moriarty said in a statement.

Asked during a press conference whether her office is concerned about potential blowback from the Trump administration, which has resisted efforts from local law enforcement to investigate federal agents who have shot and killed Minnesota residents, Moriarty said it is “not a concern of ours.”

“Our role, by the way, is to hold people accountable if they violate the laws of Minnesota,” she added. “In this particular case, we feel strongly that this agent committed second-degree assault against both of these victims. We have charged the case, and our intent is to hold them accountable.”

The Trump administration has also suggested federal agents possess “absolute immunity” from state-level prosecutions, and White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, in a statement shared by Homeland Security, has told agents that “no one” — including city and state officials — “can prevent you from fulfilling your legal obligations and duties.”

Moriarty told reporters that the administration is “wrong” to believe that agents possess absolute immunity from criminal prosecution.

The Department of Justice could, however, try to remove a state-level case to federal court, where state prosecutors could continue to press a case against the officers.

“The burden is on the agent to show that what they were doing was in the scope of their authority as a federal agent,” Moriarty said.

“Our opinion is that illegally driving on a shoulder, pulling up to a car, and pointing a gun at the heads of two community members ... is well beyond the scope of their authority as federal agents,” she said. “We will litigate that in court.”

This is a developing story

A federal judge once again demanded the Trump administration pause construction on much of the White House ballroom, but clarified that any construction related to national security and safety could continue, after lawyers for the government argued the building “implicates the personal safety” of the president.

District Court Judge Richard Leon, who has previously expressed frustration at government lawyers in the case, accused those same attorneys of being “disingenuous” in a 10-page order Thursday that clarified above-ground construction of the ballroom is still halted.

“It is, to say the least, incredible, if not disingenuous, that Defendants now argue that my Order does not stop ballroom construction because of the safety-and-security exception,” he wrote.

Just two weeks ago, Leon ordered the Trump administration to pause construction of the White House ballroom, claiming it needed approval from Congress to erect the 90,000-sqare foot structure. Leon did, however, say any construction related to national security – such as the below-ground facility – was permitted to continue.

But lawyers for the administration asked an appeals court to prevent Leon’s order from taking effect because the construction was imperative to the safety of the president. The appeals court granted their request and asked Leon to consider the national security implications.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Leon said the administration’s latest assertions were a direct contradiction of their previous claims that the below-ground work on a military-grade bunker was separate from the above-ground construction of the actual ballroom.

Last month, the president told reporters the military was involved in building a “big complex” under the $400 million structure – potentially akin to the Presidential Emergency Operations Center, which was originally under the East Wing. He indicated the bunker would include “major medical facilities,” a “hospital” and “bomb shelters.”

Lawyers for the government have repeatedly argued that the national security elements of the ballroom construction made it imperative to continue, including below-ground construction.

But in his original ruling, Leon rejected their sweeping argument, saying “the existence of a ‘large hole’ beside the White House is, of course, a problem of the President’s own making!”

Leon did permit “construction necessary to ensure the safety and security of the White House” to continue.

open image in gallery Without congressional approval, the White House tore down the East Wing of the White House in October to make room for the $400 million ballroom ( Getty )

But that exception was not enough, lawyers for the government told an appeals court.

Leon rejected their claim once again in Thursday’s order.

“I previously rejected Defendants' argument that ‘any construction delay will undermine national security’ because - and here is the bottom line - Defendants themselves forged ahead and created this ‘coordinated and managed safety hazard’ on White House grounds,” Leon said.

“In my view, these arguments fail to justify Defendants' extraordinary, if not disingenuous, reading of my preliminary injunction Order,” the judge wrote.

Leon clarified that any construction related to necessary structural integrity or safety was still permitted, including “waterproofing, water management, structural reinforcement, and sealing off exposed construction areas” so long as it does not “lock in” the above-ground ballroom

He added that below-ground construction, and any above-ground work necessary to cover, secure or protect the below-ground facility, was allowed.

“I will close by noting that I have no desire or intention to be dragooned into the role of construction manager,” Leon concluded.
